claim_boundary: Metadata-only taxonomy mapping for future validation planning. It does not contain raw malware, execute exploits, replay live attacker traffic, measure TPR/FPR, or prove production detection quality.

taxonomy.benchmark_intent: Map file/model malware detection work to benchmark lanes without promoting local bootstrap or parity smoke into production claims.

mapped_validation_surfaces.scope_note: Local calibrated bootstrap and ONNX parity evidence are profile-scoped and do not establish field malware detection quality.
Schema validates benchmark report shape and guardrails, not real sample lineage or production classifier performance.

missing_requirements: Governed malware/goodware corpus with reproducible lineage and sample counts
Holdout metrics with FPR/FNR, score orientation, threshold source, and artifact hashes
Agent/server alert path evidence from non-synthetic detections
taxonomy.future_validation_gate: Require governed dataset manifest plus ML-1 through ML-3 reports before publishing malware detection quality claims.

taxonomy.benchmark_intent: Track commercial-spyware and credential-stealer behaviors separately from generic malware so future validation can test collection, exfiltration, persistence, and privacy-preserving signals.

mapped_validation_surfaces.scope_note: Replay fixtures include metadata-only tamper and exfiltration-shaped signals, not observed spyware or stealer samples.

missing_requirements: Benign and malicious credential-access scenarios with consented lab instrumentation
Negative controls for password managers, browser sync, and enterprise DLP agents
Evidence that collector privacy mode preserves required fields without collecting secrets
taxonomy.future_validation_gate: Require lab replay plus benign-control false-positive review before claiming spyware or stealer coverage.

taxonomy.benchmark_intent: Reserve a benchmark bucket for unknown-exploit behavior without implying detection of undisclosed vulnerabilities.

mapped_validation_surfaces.scope_note: Existing coverage positioning distinguishes runtime evidence from rule content but does not prove unknown-exploit detection.

missing_requirements: Behavior-only scenarios that do not depend on known CVE labels
Runtime collector evidence for exploit-like process, memory, network, or persistence chains
False-positive controls showing benign crash, updater, and automation activity are not over-promoted
taxonomy.future_validation_gate: Require behavior-chain replay with runtime evidence and FP controls; never present this as zero-day exploit prevention.

taxonomy.benchmark_intent: Separate known-CVE exploit delivery and post-exploitation behavior from generic malware and zero-day language.

mapped_validation_surfaces.scope_note: Planning artifacts can define expected event contracts, but current mapping has no CVE-scoped exploit replay evidence.

missing_requirements: CVE-scoped lab scenario with patched/unpatched or simulated-vulnerable target lineage
Exploit delivery, exploitation, and post-exploitation phases separated in expected results
Benign scanner and vulnerability-management controls to measure false positives
taxonomy.future_validation_gate: Require CVE-scoped replay package and negative controls before claiming one-day exploit coverage.

taxonomy.benchmark_intent: Track instant-messaging delivery as an ingress vector without claiming exploitation or messaging-platform protection.

mapped_validation_surfaces.scope_note: Existing replay shape can model app/web risk metadata, but it is not real IM traffic, attachment analysis, or platform integration evidence.

missing_requirements: Sanitized IM-message or attachment-delivery fixture with sender, link, attachment, and user-action metadata
Controls for benign links, enterprise chat integrations, and expected preview fetches
Runtime evidence that delivery context reaches alert/timeline without collecting message contents
taxonomy.future_validation_gate: Require metadata-only IM delivery replay and benign controls before claiming IM exploit-delivery coverage.
